summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Q1 (depth of equity, bond and insurance markets relative to GDP), Q2 (instruments to mobilise domestic and diaspora savings) and Q3 (regulatory limits on foreign portfolio participation) are pending. Leads: SEBON site and a SEBON Quarterly Securities Market Indicators PDF (surfaced by the single search), NEPSE (general knowledge), NRB CME releases and FSR Issue 17 (NEPSE capitalisation, capital-market and insurance risk sections), Nepal Insurance Authority (general knowledge; not in source catalog), MoF Economic Survey 2082/83 (capital market, insurance, savings chapters), PDMO debt bulletin and MTDS (domestic bond market and investor base), NRB Foreign Employment Saving Bond notices and user guide, ICAN FY2083/84 budget highlights (reported diaspora/offshore NPR bond proposals - to trace to the Budget Speech), NRB Foreign Investment and Loan Management Bylaw, FXM directives and the Nepal Law Commission for FITTA 2019 and Securities Act. Savings: WDI gross domestic/national savings codes (general knowledge) vs MoF/NSO. No numbers are reported; market-capitalisation figures seen in search snippets were deliberately not used.

findings.claim: Q1: NEPSE market capitalisation (NPR) at FY-end and latest, and as percent of nominal GDP.
findings.note: Market cap is a price-driven stock; ratio to FY GDP uses NSO nominal GDP (C-01). Record NRB CME and SEBON values separately (different cut-off dates). Lead URLs: https://www.sebon.gov.np/uploads/uploads/xJyc1r7uimjK2XBhBt8LWQ1K85asUqkhCJWp5Qg0.pdf; https://www.nrb.org.np/contents/uploads/2026/08/Current-Macroeconomic-and-Financial-Situation-English-1.pdf; https://www.nrb.org.np/contents/uploads/2025/08/Current-Macroeconomic-and-Financial-Situation-English-Based-on-Annual-data-of-2024.25.pdf; https://www.nepalstock.com; https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/NPL/indicator/CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS?format=json&per_page=200

findings.claim: Q3: Legal limits on foreign portfolio investment in listed Nepali securities (eligibility of foreign institutional investors, NRNs, caps, approval and repatriation rules) - verbatim provisions with dates.
findings.note: FITTA 2019, Securities Act, SEBON regulations, NRB Foreign Investment and Loan Management Bylaw and FXM directives. No rule is asserted here. Lead URLs: https://www.lawcommission.gov.np; https://www.nrb.org.np/contents/uploads/2019/12/NRB-Foreign-Investment-and-Loan-Management-Bylaw_English-2.pdf; https://www.nrb.org.np/departments/fxm/; https://www.sebon.gov.np; https://www.nrb.org.np/red/survey-report-on-foreign-direct-investment-2023-24/
findings.period: statutes and directives in force as of retrieval

findings.claim: Q2 candidate instruments (options to evaluate, not recommendations): (a) redesigned diaspora bonds (USD- or NPR-denominated, digital subscription via remittance channels); (b) offshore NPR-linked bonds; (c) infrastructure/hydropower project bonds and green bonds; (d) mutual funds and specialised investment funds with NRN access; (e) expanded contractual savings (EPF, CIT, Social Security Fund) allocation to long-term instruments; (f) remittance-linked savings accounts with long-term deposit products. Each requires uptake evidence, cost vs alternatives, FX-risk allocation and legal feasibility (Q3).
findings.note: Options list only; uptake and cost evidence pending.

findings.claim: Trade-off note: channelling remittance savings into long-term domestic assets raises investment capacity but concentrates household and bank exposure to domestic asset prices; FX-denominated diaspora bonds shift currency risk to the government under the peg. To be reported under welfare objectives, not optimised for GDP alone.

Market capitalisation/GDP is a valuation measure driven by prices and a bank-dominated listing base; it is not by itself evidence of long-term financing capacity. Primary-issuance flows (equity, debentures) are the preferred depth indicator for investment mobilisation.

data_gaps: No SEBON, NEPSE, NIA, PDMO or NRB file downloaded in r1; all values pending.
Nepal Insurance Authority is not in research/sources/source_catalog.yaml; request 00A to add it (tier 1) - leads tagged with 'academic' source_id as a placeholder.
Budget Speech FY2083/84 (2026/27) direct file not located; diaspora/offshore bond proposals known only via a secondary summary (ICAN).
Statutory texts (FITTA 2019, Securities Act, SEBON regulations on foreign institutional investors) not located as direct files; Law Commission URL is general knowledge.
Contractual savings institutions (EPF, CIT, SSF) portfolio data not located; not in source catalog.
Several leads (NEPSE, NIA, Law Commission, WDI savings and market-cap codes) are from general knowledge and marked unverified.

assumptions.text: Market depth ratios use NSO FY nominal GDP as denominator and FY-end stocks; WDI CY-labelled ratios are cross-checks only.
Savings-mobilisation options are evaluated, not endorsed; any recommendation requires uptake evidence and audit by Agents 15/28.
Foreign portfolio rules are treated as those in force on the retrieval date; pending amendments are listed separately.

challenges.text: 03C and 23E share diaspora-finance leads (FESB, NRN IPO quota, NRB FI bylaw, ICAN budget highlights); propose 23E owns diaspora demand/uptake evidence and 03C owns market-structure and regulatory limits to avoid double extraction.
Add Nepal Insurance Authority, Nepal Stock Exchange and contractual savings funds (EPF, CIT, SSF) to the source catalog so leads can carry proper source ids.
Do not use market capitalisation/GDP as a proxy for investment-financing capacity in the US$3T arithmetic; use primary issuance and bank credit capacity (03B) instead.

uncertainty: High. No value retrieved. Market capitalisation is highly price-volatile and cut-off dates differ across SEBON, NEPSE and NRB; insurance data depend on a regulator not yet catalogued; legal limits on foreign portfolio investment must be read verbatim and may have recent amendments; savings ratios differ between domestic and national concepts and between FY and CY sources.

market_depth_table.question: What is the depth of equity, bond and insurance markets relative to GDP?
market_depth_table.method: Extract FY-end stocks from SEBON/NRB/PDMO/NIA; divide by NSO FY nominal GDP; record WDI CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS and NY.GDS.TOTL.ZS as CY cross-checks; peer comparison (South Asia) only with same-source data.

regulatory_constraints.question: What regulatory limits constrain foreign portfolio participation?
items_to_extract: eligibility of foreign institutional investors in secondary market
NRN participation rules and quotas in IPOs
minimum investment / approval requirements under FITTA 2019 and FI bylaw
repatriation and FX conversion rules (NRB FXM)
sectoral foreign-ownership caps (e.g. banking, insurance) where set by sector regulators
regulatory_constraints.method: Quote provisions verbatim with instrument, section and date; classify as statutory vs regulatory vs directive; note pending amendments.
